paper.title_en: Dynamics and radiative properties of thin accretion disks around nonlinear magnetically charged AdS black holes with quintessence and dark matter
paper.abstract_en: We study the dynamics of circular orbits and the thermal properties of a thin accretion disk around a nonlinear magnetically charged anti-de Sitter black hole surrounded by quintessence and perfect fluid dark matter (PFDM). We characterize the circular-orbit dynamics through the effective potential, the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO), and the radial and vertical epicyclic frequencies, and investigate the disk emission within the Novikov-Thorne framework. This analysis reveals that the PFDM and quintessence parameters modify the location of the ISCO and the properties of circular motion, while the influence of the nonlinear magnetic charge is more pronounced in the strong-field region. In particular, increasing the PFDM parameter shifts the ISCO inward, enhances the radial epicyclic frequency, and reduces the vertical epicyclic frequency. Increasing the quintessence state parameter ϵ from more negative to less negative values also shifts the ISCO inward and enhances both epicyclic frequencies, whereas increasing the quintessence normalization parameter cq moves the ISCO outward. The radiative flux and disk temperature are also modified by the PFDM and quintessence parameters, while the nonlinear magnetic charge mainly affects the inner region of the accretion disk. These results infer how surrounding matter fields and nonlinear electromagnetic effects alter the strong-field dynamics and thermal emission of accretion disks around the considered black hole.
